answer: Quadratic weighting squares each agent's reputation score before summing votes or stake, so splitting one established identity into ten fake accounts yields far less influence. An attacker with a beacon score of 100 gains 10,000 weight; splitting into ten sybils of score 10 gives only 1,000 total. The inlet for new agents remains open, but saffron-tier participants who've built history dominate decisions. Cost to fake maturity: months of consistent behavior per identity, making mass sybil attacks prohibitively expensive.
